lines.trans: Take the lower panes, Nour; Rami and I can reach the top arch from the ladder.
Dip the sponge in warm water with a drop of vinegar—zero streaks on old glass!
Whoa, look at that first square I wiped! Blue sky and green leaves!
Remember when mom made us wash the kitchen windows every spring, Rami?
You always splashed water on my shirt and blamed the wind!
Careful up there, you two—keep the soapy water in the bucket!
Look through the clean glass now: you can see the whole courtyard lantern line!
When we open the outside shutters tomorrow, sunlight will pour across all four tables.
Wait—Rami, didn't you say your train home leaves tonight at seven?
I called my studio partner and moved my ticket to Saturday morning.
Really?! You are staying in Amman until Friday's opening night?!
Nothing could pull me away before Room Nine opens!

أجّل.gloss: to postpone; move to a later date

meanings.en: to postpone; move to a later date
meanings.note: Form II Jordanian verb; spoken text omits shadda (أجلت تذكرتي 'I postponed my ticket').

examples.trans: We moved the meeting to Wednesday morning.

examples.text: رامي أجل تذكرته عشان يحضر الافتتاح.
examples.trans: Rami moved his ticket so he could attend the opening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: With 1sg suffix أمي (ummi), affectionately means 'Mom' even when talking to a sibling ('our mom').

examples.text: أمي علمتني أعمل شوربة عدس بالليمون.
examples.trans: Mom taught me how to make lentil soup with lemon.

examples.text: كل جمعة بنزور بيت أمي بعمان.
examples.trans: Every Friday we visit my mom's house in Amman.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Soft cleaning sponge for washing windows or dishes.

examples.text: اعصري الإسفنجة منيح قبل ما تمسحي القزاز.
examples.trans: Wring the sponge out well before wiping the glass.
We bought two new sponges for the café kitchen.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Official opening day or evening of a café, exhibition, or hall.

examples.text: افتتاح الكافيه رح يكون بآخر الأسبوع.
examples.trans: The café opening will take place at the end of the week.

examples.text: عزمنا كل الجيران على ليلة الافتتاح.
examples.trans: We invited all the neighbours to opening night.

meanings.note: The holy day in Islam and the weekend in Jordan.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: The day of the week, Saturday.

examples.text: كل سبت الصبح بنمشي عسوق الحارة.
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning we walk to the neighbourhood market.

examples.text: الخبز الطازة بيجهز يوم السبت الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Fresh bread is ready on Saturday at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Levantine relational adjective formed from تحت ('under/below') + -aani; opposite of فوقاني.

examples.trans: The tuning wrench is in the bottom drawer.

examples.text: نور مسحت الألواح التحتانية للشباك الكبير.
examples.trans: Nour wiped the lower panes of the tall window.

meanings.note: Train, bus, or concert ticket.

examples.text: حجزت تذكرة قطار ليوم السبت الصبح.
examples.trans: I booked a train ticket for Saturday morning.

examples.text: حطيت التذاكر بجيبتي عشان ما تضيع.
examples.trans: I put the tickets in my pocket so they wouldn't get lost.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتذكر, بيتذكر).

examples.trans: Remember your three simple sentences.
I can remember them easily.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian expression to express surprise or ask for confirmation, like 'really?' or 'seriously!'.

examples.trans: My grandfather's workshop was on this street.
Did you really finish all the work?

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Describes outer shutters, doors, or walls facing the courtyard or street.

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش الخارجي بلون أخضر دافي.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the outside shutters a warm green.

examples.text: الباب الخارجي بيفتح مباشرة على شارع الياسمين.
examples.trans: The exterior gate opens straight onto Jasmine Street.

meanings.note: Can mean a physical line, a phone line, a bus route, or handwriting.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

meanings.note: Household vinegar used both in cooking and for streak-free window washing.

examples.text: نقطة خل بالمي الدافية بتخلي القزاز يلمع.
examples.trans: A drop of vinegar in warm water makes the glass sparkle.

examples.text: حطيت شوية زيت زيتون وخل عالسلطة.
examples.trans: I dressed the salad with a little olive oil and vinegar.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of دائما ('always').

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.
Noon traffic is always slow.

meanings.note: One of the four seasons: صيف summer, خريف autumn, شتا winter, ربيع spring.

examples.trans: Spring in Amman is short and lovely.
In spring we go out to the hills.

meanings.note: Instance noun (ism marra) from رجع ('return').

examples.text: قطار الرجعة بيطلع من المحطة الساعة سبعة.
examples.trans: The return train leaves the station at seven o'clock.

examples.text: بطريق الرجعة من السوق، اشترينا نعنع أخضر.
examples.trans: On the way back from the market, we bought fresh green mint.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Geminate verb used for splashing water or sprinkling herbs/sugar.

examples.trans: I sprinkled a little water on the flowers in the morning.

examples.text: سلمى رشت قرفة مطحونة فوق الكيكة.
examples.trans: Salma dusted ground cinnamon over the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Numeral 'seven' (عالسبعة 'at seven o'clock').

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I booked room seven yesterday.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a water or paint bucket (plural سطول stuul).

examples.text: جهزنا سطلين مي دافية عشان نغسل الشبابيك.
examples.trans: We got two buckets of warm water ready to wash the windows.

examples.text: انتبه لا يوقع سطل الصابون عن الدرج.
examples.trans: Careful the bucket of soapy water doesn't tip off the step.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سلالم.

examples.trans: He played the musical scale slowly.
He climbed the ladder to fit the bulb.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سماوات.

examples.trans: The evening sky is clear and calm.
The lanterns are glowing beneath the sky.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: شريكة). Plural: شركاء.

examples.trans: Great work today, partner!

examples.text: همه شركاء بالمخبز من عشر سنين.
examples.trans: They have been partners in the bakery for ten years.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite no -a ending.

examples.trans: The warm sun came out after the rain.
Read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Levantine word for slatted window shutters, used as a collective: الشيش مسكر 'the shutters are closed'.

examples.trans: Close the shutters, the sun is strong.
Green shutters suit the house.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: There is clean soap and a towel in the bathroom.
The scent of olive soap is natural.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صفوف.

examples.trans: We sat in the front row at the concert.
The chairs are arranged in two rows.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian hollow verb (بطال / بنطال) meaning 'reach a high shelf or latch'.

examples.text: ما بقدر أطال الرف الفوقاني بدون سلم.
examples.trans: I can't reach the top shelf without a ladder.

examples.text: بعدنا الغصن وهلا بنطال الشنكل بسهولة.
examples.trans: We moved the branch aside and now we can reach the hook easily.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: Form II طلّع means both 'look!' (طلّع بالمراية) and 'bring/carry up' (رح أطلّع الشنتة).

examples.text: طلع بالمراية ورا المكتب يا معلم!
examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk, boss!
I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Form II Jordanian verb for filling buckets, cups, or rooms with light.

examples.trans: We filled the two buckets with warm soapy water.
Morning sunlight fills the room with brightness.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Wash dishes, clothes, windows or your hands.

examples.trans: I washed the cups and put them on the shelf.
Wash your hands before eating.

meanings.note: Form II verb meaning 'dip a sponge in water or dunk bread/biscuits in tea'.

examples.text: غطست الإسفنجة بالمي الدافية ومسحت اللوح.
examples.trans: I dipped the sponge in warm water and wiped the pane.

examples.text: بحب أغطس البسكوت بكاسة الشاي السخن.
examples.trans: I love dipping biscuits in a glass of hot tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فوقانية, plural: فوقانيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
The red ribbon is in the top pocket.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قطارات.

examples.trans: The grandfather carved a small wooden train.
Children love playing with trains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قمصان.

examples.trans: He put on a neat, ironed white shirt.
He changed his shirt twice before the appointment.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقواس.

examples.text: ادخل عالساحة من هاد القوس الحجري.
examples.trans: Step into the courtyard through this stone arch.

examples.text: الأقواس القديمة مبنية من حجر عمان.
examples.trans: The old arches are built of Amman limestone.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Hollow verb (laam / biluum) meaning 'blame someone or something'.

examples.text: لا تلوم الهوا إذا طارت الورقة عن الطاولة!
examples.trans: Don't blame the wind if the sheet flew off the table!

examples.text: ما بنلوم مازن لو توتر قبل التفتيش.
examples.trans: We can't blame Mazen for feeling nervous before the inspection.

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Denotes a square shape or a square area in geometry or real-world objects.

examples.text: أول مربع قزاز مسحناه بين السما الزرقا وراه.
examples.trans: The first glass square we wiped revealed the blue sky behind it.

examples.text: بلاط الساحة مقسم لمربعات حجر مرتبة.
examples.trans: The courtyard paving is laid out in neat stone squares.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مستحيلة, plural: —).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
It is impossible for us to forget this week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسح, بيمسح).

examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate.
We wiped down the tables before breakfast.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Used for both a workplace (office) and the piece of furniture (desk).

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for clean or tidy.

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the room is ready.

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water onto your clean floor.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical dot, a score point, or a drop of liquid.

examples.trans: Not a single drop of juice got on the table!

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من الشوربة السخنة.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the hot soup.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
